title: Lockout/tagout: the full procedure and why each step exists
summary: A training overview of energy control, verification and release; the machine-specific written procedure governs.

blocks.title: Lockout/tagout, whole and in order
blocks.body: Unexpected startup and stored energy can injure during service. Authorized employees follow the site’s energy-control program and machine-specific procedure. This is a learning outline, not a complete procedure for an unidentified machine or electrical task.

blocks.heading: The procedure, in order
items: Prepare: identify every hazardous energy source and the approved isolation method; notify affected employees.
Shut down normally, then operate the specified energy-isolating devices. A stop button or software command is not isolation.
Apply lockout/tagout under the written procedure, including the approved group arrangement when needed.
Relieve, restrain or otherwise render stored energy safe. Continue verification if hazardous energy can reaccumulate.
Verify isolation and de-energization before work. Return attempted operating controls to their safe/off position. Electrical testing requires qualified personnel and the appropriate procedure.
Work only within the verified conditions; reassess if the task or conditions change.

blocks.heading: Why each step exists
rows: Identify all sources and affected people
Prevent movement, pressure release or other residual-energy hazards
Establish the required safe condition before exposure
Confirm equipment and people are ready before restoration

blocks.title: Your lock is your life insurance
blocks.body: Normally the employee who applied a device removes it. Removal in that employee’s absence requires the employer’s specific documented procedure, including verifying absence, reasonable contact efforts, and ensuring the employee knows before returning to work. It is not an informal supervisor override.

blocks.heading: Coming back to service, in order
items: Inspect the equipment and work area; remove nonessential items and confirm components are intact.
Ensure people are safely positioned or removed and controls are in the required state.
Remove devices under the written removal procedure.
After device removal and before startup, notify affected employees that devices have been removed.
Restore and restart using the machine-specific procedure; do not assume it is simply isolation in reverse.

blocks.heading: When more than one person is on the machine
blocks.body: Group lockout must provide equivalent personal protection through the approved procedure, often using a group lockbox. Shift changes require an orderly transfer that maintains protection. Each worker does not necessarily place a lock on every individual isolator.

blocks.title: Use the actual procedure
blocks.body: If the procedure does not cover the machine, energy source or task, stop and resolve the gap with the responsible authorized person.
